content.title: About
content.content: Applesauce is a ready‑to‑eat product made by cooking and pureeing ripe apples without added sugar. It has a smooth, uniform texture, a mild sweet‑tart flavor, and the fresh aroma of apples.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Applesauce is often used as a base for baby foods because of its soft texture and natural sweetness.
More than 2 million tonnes of applesauce are produced annually in the United States.
Traditionally, families made applesauce at home by baking apples and mashing them.
Applesauce can be plain or flavored with cinnamon, vanilla, or a small amount of sugar.
The aroma of applesauce retains much of the vitamins and antioxidants found in fresh apples.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Applesauce provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: The puree retains both soluble and insoluble fibers that aid digestion and help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: One hundred grams of applesauce contain about 45 kcal, making it a light snack option.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Pectin and polyphenols present in the puree have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to apples, ranging from mild itching to more severe symptoms.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: While original applesauce contains no added sugar, many commercial brands add sugar, increasing its calorie count.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some brands use preservatives such as potassium sorbate to extend shelf life; those sensitive to additives should choose preservative‑free versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Applesauce can be enjoyed on its own, mixed into oatmeal, yogurt, smoothies, baked goods, or used as a filling for pancakes and crepes. It is also commonly served as a side dish with pork or poultry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store an opened container of applesauce in the refrigerator in a sealed jar for up to 5‑7 days. Unopened packages should be kept in a cool, dry place away from direct light.
